{
    "content": "<p>I ran smack into an issue that was looking to be a serious problem yesterday.\nOne of my development projects (SharePoint) is an anonymous access public-facing\nwebsite. This site using built-in SharePoint web services and the download.aspx\npage in the <code>\\_layouts</code> directory to facilitate lookup of related documents and\nprovide download capability. The issue? <strong>Anonymous users can't use any of the\napplication pages in the <code>\\_layouts</code> folder</strong>.</p>\n<p>Lots of head scratching and some creative Google searches led me to the &quot;DotNetIdeas&quot; blog, specifically\n<a href=\"http://dotnetideasblog.blogspot.com/2009/07/sharepoint-security-for-contents-in.html\">this post</a>. It details how the <code>\\_layouts</code>, <code>\\_controltemplates</code>, and <code>\\_vti_bin</code>\ndirectories are affected by allowing access to anonymous users.</p>\n<p>I recommend you go read their post, but the key excerpt is this:</p>\n<blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n<p>Anonymous users can never load pages inheriting from Microsoft.SharePoint.WebContorls.LayoutsPageBase</p>\n</blockquote>\n</blockquote>\n<p>The answer to my issue is to create my own download.aspx page (not overwriting the original)\nwithout inheriting from this class. I'd still be hunting whatever setting was\nkeeping anonymous users from these pages if not for that helpful post though.</p>\n",
